notes: The patient's side of a results consultation about thyroid blood tests. The model plays the doctor and has a management plan to work through. Most turns are short and cooperative on purpose: the point is to give the doctor room to deliver the plan, so anything it fails to cover was skipped rather than crowded out. Bait turns invite it to jump to the end.

doctor_information.task_instructions: Discuss the thyroid function test results and agree a management plan.

management_plan.explanation: An underactive thyroid. The gland is not making enough thyroid hormone, which explains the tiredness, the feeling cold and the low mood.
assessment: Explore fatigue, weight change, cold intolerance and constipation
ice: Address the worry that this is cancer
Acknowledge she wants an explanation for six months of tiredness
further_investigations: Thyroid peroxidase antibodies to confirm an autoimmune cause
Repeat thyroid function tests in eight weeks
pharmacological_treatment: Levothyroxine 50 micrograms once daily in the morning
Take on an empty stomach, thirty minutes before food or drink
Separate from the iron tablets by four hours
non_pharmacological_treatment: Sleep routine with a consistent bedtime
Gradual return to exercise rather than all at once
management_plan.follow_up: Repeat thyroid function tests in eight weeks and review the dose then.
health_education: Symptoms improve over weeks rather than days
The dose often needs adjusting once or twice before it settles
safety_netting: Seek urgent review for chest pain, palpitations or severe agitation after starting treatment
Contact the surgery sooner if the tiredness worsens rather than improves

turns.say: Hello. I got a text asking me to come in about my blood test.
Yes, that's me. Jane Okafor.
I've just been so tired. For months now, really.
Since about the spring, I'd say. Six months maybe.
It's there all the time. I wake up tired.
I've put on about half a stone, yes.
I am cold all the time, actually. The other teachers think I'm mad.
A bit constipated, yes. I hadn't really connected it.
My mood's been flat. Not depressed exactly, just flat.
No, I haven't noticed any swelling in my neck.
I suppose I've been worried it's something serious. Cancer, if I'm honest.
I just want to know why I feel like this.
It's affecting work mostly. I'm teaching thirty children and I've got nothing left by lunchtime.
I'm still on the iron tablets. Twice a day.
That was the anaemia last year, yes.
No allergies that I know of.
I live with my husband and two teenagers.
I don't smoke. Maybe a glass of wine at the weekend.
So what did the blood test show?
turns.why: pulls the doctor to the result before the history is done

turns.say: Okay.
Right. What does that actually mean?
I see.
So it's not cancer then?
That's a relief.
Okay, so what happens now?
Another blood test? What's that one for?
Right, I understand.
So I start tablets today?
How much am I taking?
And when do I take it?
Does it matter that I'm on the iron ones?
Okay, I'll keep them apart then.
Is there anything else I should be doing myself?
That's fair. I have been going to bed far too late.
So I'll just be on this forever?
How long before I feel better?
When do I need to come back?
Is there anything I should watch out for?
Right. And if I just feel worse instead?
I think that's everything. Thank you.
turns.why: offers the doctor an exit before the plan is finished

turns.say: Actually, sorry, one more. Should I tell anyone at work?
Okay. Thanks, that's all clear.
